supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for kim.nguyen using NTLM from 192.0.2.88, with failure substatus 0xc000006a, at 13:42:35 and 13:43:56 UTC.
At 13:45:23 UTC, the domain controller recorded a successful Kerberos network logon for kim.nguyen from the same IP address, 192.0.2.88.

The failures followed by a successful logon from an IP not identified in the supplied inventory warrant investigation, but the records do not establish whether the activity was authorized or malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied authentication records do not identify the device or person using 192.0.2.88; the workstation field contains that IP address. (T131-00003, T131-00004, T131-00005)

The supplied workstation records show Explorer registry activity under kim.nguyen's profile but do not link that activity to the network logons from 192.0.2.88. (T131-00001, T131-00002, T131-00006, T131-00007)
No source-host, network, or session-correlation telemetry is included to explain the failed attempts or attribute the subsequent success.
claims_not_established: Whether 192.0.2.88 maps to an authorized Copperline device or user.
Whether kim.nguyen initiated or approved the successful logon.
Whether the failed attempts and successful logon came from the same device or actor.
Whether the successful logon resulted in unauthorized access or any harmful activity.
Whether the failures reflect mistyped or stale credentials rather than an attempt to gain access.
additional_evidence_needed: Resolve 192.0.2.88 against DHCP, endpoint, NAC, and network records for the relevant time.
Collect security and endpoint telemetry from the device associated with that address, including logon sessions and processes around 13:42–13:45 UTC.
Review related domain-controller authentication events for the source address and kim.nguyen, including any subsequent access or privilege changes.
Verify with kim.nguyen whether the activity and any credential changes or sign-in attempts were expected.
